newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Germany sees no consensus on EMU stability pact.
newsitem.headline: Germany sees no consensus on EMU stability pact.

text.p: European finance ministers reached no agreement on a pact to ensure stable budgets for countries participating in economic and monetary union after the single currency starts in 1999, German Economic State Secretary Juergen Stark said on Monday.

Germany held to its original proposal for strong sanctions against countries that fail to keep their budgets in line and numerical definitions of the exceptional cases that would allow countries to avoid those sanctions, he said.
Stark said the content of the hoped-for consensus was more important that reaching by a specific deadline.
The EU has been hoping to agree a post-EMU stability pact by the summit of EU leaders in Dublin on December 13 and 14. - Brussels Newsroom -- +32 2 287-6830
